questions.text: What is a zoning ordinance in the CLUP system?

options.text: The enforceable local legislative tool that implements the CLUP.
A nonbinding sketch prepared by a developer.
A national building-code table that replaces the CLUP.
A mayoral memo that never needs Sanggunian action.

questions.rationale: RPS and RA 7160 frame the zoning ordinance as the enforceable implementation of the CLUP.
questions.explanation: Zoning works through inclusion and exclusion. It enables certain uses in designated zones (e.g., 'residential use is permitted here') while prohibiting the same uses elsewhere (e.g., 'residential use is prohibited in the industrial zone'). This dual mechanism guides where development happens and where it does not. Zoning allocates land use; pollution control is separate regulation (environmental law). Zoning does not control environmental impacts directly. Zoning is a neutral regulatory mechanism applicable to all properties. While zoning can have inequitable outcomes (e.g., zoning out affordable housing), that is a policy problem, not the inherent function of zoning. Building permits are issued under zoning authority, but they are a separate approval. Design standards are also separate from zoning (though related). Zoning works through inclusion and exclusion. It enables certain uses in designated zones (e.g., 'residential use is permitted here') while prohibiting the same uses elsewhere (e.g., 'residential use is prohibited in the industrial zone'). This dual mechanism guides where development happens and where it does not. Zoning enables development in designated zones; restrains it in others. This allocation mechanism is zoning's core function.

questions.text: Who has authority to enact integrated zoning ordinances for a municipality?

options.text: The Sangguniang Bayan.
The MPDC acting alone.
DHSUD acting as the local council.
A private surveyor.

questions.rationale: RA 7160 grants the municipal Sanggunian power to enact integrated zoning ordinances.

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes CLUP from zoning ordinance?

options.text: The CLUP sets spatial policy; the zoning ordinance makes enforceable use and development controls.
The CLUP and zoning ordinance are identical documents with no legal difference.
The zoning ordinance is only an illustration.
The CLUP is prepared only by private developers.

questions.rationale: The CLUP is the plan; the zoning ordinance is the statutory implementation tool.

questions.text: If a zoning ordinance conflicts with the approved CLUP, what is the source-safe concern?

options.text: It is vulnerable because zoning should be in consonance with the approved CLUP.
It is automatically valid because zoning never follows CLUP.
It is irrelevant because only the mayor decides land use.
It becomes a national law.

questions.rationale: RA 7160 says integrated zoning ordinances are enacted in consonance with the approved CLUP.

questions.text: Which items are normally ordinance-specific rather than universal defaults?

options.text: FAR, lot coverage, setbacks, height limits, parking, and conditional uses.
The existence of RA 7160.
The existence of the Sanggunian.
The fact that LGUs prepare CLUPs.

questions.rationale: Dimensional and use standards come from the adopted zoning ordinance unless another source is specified.
questions.code_citation: Land use planning principles; CLUP and zoning strategy

questions.text: Which planning actor supplies technical content for zoning?

options.text: The local planning and technical structure, such as the CPDC/MPDC and technical working groups.
The Sanggunian alone with no technical input.
Only private brokers.
Only a national court.

questions.rationale: RPS describes technical components that supply planning data and analysis.
questions.code_citation: Mixed-use zoning best practices; New Urbanism principles

questions.text: Which planning actor makes the legislative zoning decision?

options.text: The Sanggunian.
The zoning applicant.
The drafting technician alone.
The fire inspector alone.

questions.rationale: The Sanggunian is the legislative body with zoning enactment authority.
questions.explanation: That describes the CLUP (Comprehensive Land Use Plan), not the zoning ordinance. The CLUP is the vision; the ordinance is the law that implements it. The Zoning Ordinance is a legislative tool adopted by the Sanggunian that translates CLUP decisions into enforceable rules specifying what uses are allowed in each zone, building height limits, setbacks, lot sizes, and other regulations. The Planning Office drafts the zoning ordinance, but the Sanggunian must formally adopt it as law. Guidelines alone are not enforceable. DHSUD reviews the ordinance for conformity with national standards, but the ordinance itself is not a construction permit—it sets the rules under which permits are issued. The Zoning Ordinance is a legislative tool adopted by the Sanggunian that translates CLUP decisions into enforceable rules specifying what uses are allowed in each zone, building height limits, setbacks, lot sizes, and other regulations. Zoning Ordinance = enforceable legislative act adopted by Sanggunian, implementing the CLUP.

questions.text: What does the HLURB CLUP Guidebook say a CLUP should integrate?

options.text: Sectoral plans and policies for land-use categories such as settlements, production, protection, and infrastructure.
Only architectural facade styles.
Only the preferences of one landowner.
Only annual payroll records.

questions.rationale: The Guidebook describes CLUP integration of sectoral plans and land-use categories.

questions.text: Why should a zoning answer not invent an R-zone numeric limit when the item does not provide it?

options.text: Because local zoning standards are ordinance-specific and must be read from the applicable ordinance.
Because zoning never has numeric standards.
Because the CLUP cancels all numbers.
Because only national defaults exist.

questions.rationale: Numeric zoning controls must be anchored to the local ordinance or stated facts.

questions.text: Which source-safe answer applies when a proposed use is not permitted by the zoning ordinance?

options.text: It cannot proceed as proposed unless a valid ordinance procedure allows variance, conditional use, rezoning, or amendment.
It automatically proceeds if profitable.
It proceeds if the planning office verbally agrees.
It proceeds because CLUPs are advisory only.

questions.rationale: The zoning ordinance is enforceable; conflicts require a lawful local process.
